payload.claim: `restore_mutant` requires `mutant.replace`'s bytes to occur in the file exactly once, but `Mutant.replace` defaults to `""` and carries no validator forbidding empty replace (saffron/intake.py:62), unlike `find`. For any non-empty file, `content.count(b"")` equals `len(content) + 1`, which is never 1, so restoring a mutant whose `replace` is empty (an ordinary mutation-testing operator: deleting a guard, a clamp, a statement) always raises `MutationError`, even though `apply_mutant` happily applied it moments earlier. This breaks the documented round-trip contract ('Applying and restoring leaves the file byte-identical', one of this spec's own acceptance criteria) for a value the schema explicitly permits by default, and no test in tests/test_mutation.py exercises `replace=""` so the defect is invisible to every gate and to census/criteria.
